recommendation: Keep the fix. If Common Languages is to become normative in the future, record an explicit work-group decision because FHIR-13732 intentionally made the starter/preferred Common Languages value set non-normative.
issue_request: FHIR-13732 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The work group rejected merging the larger submitted language list, changed the Language binding so implementers could use codes in the maximum/all-language BCP-47 value set, and directed that the preferred Common Languages value set be non-normative while maximum bindings for normative elements be normative.
initial_application: Jira's svn revision 14714 maps to git commit d141f78c79b5de737def71b3d00737af2789503e, which changed the Language binding from extensible Common Languages with max All Languages to preferred Common Languages with max All Languages and added Trial-Use standards-status to valueset-languages.xml. Follow-up cleanup normalized the extension to valueCode trial-use.
additional_context: Later R6 decisions changed the binding representation to required All Languages plus starter Common Languages, which remains consistent with FHIR-13732's goal. Commit 9987f9c0c3ce5ec4f277c22ed71cbb2d210efeb6 subsequently changed Common Languages from trial-use to normative without a discovered language-specific tracker or community decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml so Common Languages again carries standards-status trial-use. No binding rows or resource StructureDefinitions were changed because the current required All Languages plus starter Common Languages pattern already reflects later applied binding-policy work.
source_changes: source/terminologies/valueset-languages.xml: changed structuredefinition-standards-status from normative to trial-use.

related_jiras.note: Applied the required All Languages plus starter Common Languages pattern to TerminologyCapabilities.language, confirming the current binding representation should be preserved.
Established the broader R6 binding policy that required bindings belong in the primary binding and starter/preferred sets can appear as additional bindings.
Later no-change decision explains that All Languages covers BCP-47 grammar, including appropriate three-character subtags, supporting the broader required binding.
